localBiteReport: Reports from this week (Oct 30–Nov 5, 2026) indicate the Choctawhatchee Bay/Destin inshore bite is in an unsettled fall transition — recent hurricane activity, warm spells, and inconsistent cold fronts have scattered both redfish and speckled trout between their summer and winter holding areas. That said, redfish remain the most reliable target, with fish actively feeding around bridges, jetties, and East Pass; a report from last week (Oct 23–29) by Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters noted that cut mullet on Carolina rigs outperformed live bait on the bay flats after a cold front pushed through. Speckled trout in the 22–27-inch range are showing up wherever bait concentrations can be located, though the bite should become more predictable once daytime highs consistently drop out of the 80s. Water temp at this location is 76°F. This is also prime timing for the fall flounder run — the annual migration of southern flounder toward the Gulf typically peaks in late October through mid-November, with the pass and Mid-Bay Bridge area among the top spots.
